samples.summary: Decrease no-op guard (`selectionRendersAt`) inspects only raw values, so a Decrease press does nothing while other selected cells visibly render decimals via their number format
samples.evidence: `changeDecimals` line 4198: `if (stepped < 0 && !explicitDp && (await this.selectionRendersAt(0))) return;`. `selectionRendersAt` (4246-4261) only looks at `cell.v` via `decimalsInValue`, never at the cell's effective `nf`/`dp`. Scenario: A1 = '12' plain (active, valueDp 0, no explicit dp) and B1 = '12' with `nf: 'number'` (renders '12.00'). Selecting A1:B1 and pressing Decrease returns early — B1 keeps showing two decimals even though it has decimals to drop. The comment on the guard explicitly claims the check "has to look past the active cell: a neighbour that still shows decimals has something to lose", but a neighbour that shows decimals only because of its format is missed.

samples.summary: `unsetKeepsRendering` formats every selected cell with the ACTIVE cell's `nf`, ignoring each cell's own effective format, so an unset can be approved that changes another cell's rendering
samples.evidence: Lines 4290-4296 compute `effective = this.resolveEffectiveStyle(...)` but use only `effective?.cu`; the comparison uses the active cell's `nf`/`nfAfter` for every cell. If the active cell has `dp` with plain/undefined `nf` (nf param undefined → both sides return the raw value, always equal) while a neighbour carries `nf: 'percent'` (or 'currency') with the same stored `dp`, the check passes and `unsetRangeStyleValues({dp})` strips that neighbour's `dp` (its style verdict is 'match' since only `dp` is requested). The neighbour then falls back to the format's default 2 decimals instead of the requested `target`, so the step silently renders it wrong (e.g. target 3 → neighbour still shows 2).

samples.summary: Unsetting the last key of a column/row/sheet style leaves an empty `{}` style layer persisted, so `getStyle` returns `{}` instead of `undefined`
samples.evidence: Lines 4435-4468 write `next` unconditionally when `omitStyleKeys` returns a value, including when `next` is `{}` (`this.colStyles.set(col, next); await this.store.setColumnStyle(col, next)`), whereas range patches (4481) drop empty styles and cells (4493) are deleted. `MemStore.setColumnStyle` (packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts:392) stores it as-is, and `resolveEffectiveStyle` (sheet.ts:883) only returns undefined when every layer is falsy — an empty object is truthy, so after a column/row/sheet round trip `getStyle` returns `{}`. The new tests acknowledge this by asserting `style?.dp`/`style?.nf` rather than `style` being undefined (test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:349-357), unlike the cell-level tests.

samples.summary: Decrease at the dp floor with an explicit dp always re-writes the same style, appending a redundant range-style patch / undo step on every press
samples.evidence: When `explicitDp` is true and `dp === 0`, `stepped = -1` → `clamped = true`, the unset branch is skipped by `!clamped`, and control falls to `await this.setRangeStyle({ dp: 0, ... })` (4231-4235) even though nothing changes. For a cell selection this goes through `addRangeStylePatch`, so repeatedly pressing Decrease at zero decimals keeps producing document writes/undo entries for a no-op.

samples.summary: `compactCell` was made spill-aware but `isEmptyCell` was not, so a spill ghost whose value is the empty string is deleted (and detached) by style-only rewrites
samples.evidence: `isEmptyCell` (style-mutation.ts:48-52) considers only `v`/`f`/`s`; `hasCellContent` treats `v === ''` as no content. The calculator writes ghosts as `{ v: values[dr]?.[dc] ?? '', spillAnchor: sref }` (calculator.ts:141), so an empty spill result yields a cell whose only surviving field is `spillAnchor`. In the new `unsetRangeStyleValues` (sheet.ts:4491-4497) and in the existing `clearCellStylesInRange` (sheet.ts:2007-2012), `compactCell` now preserves `spillAnchor` but `isEmptyCell(nextCell)` still returns true, so the store deletes the ghost — losing the spill link the diff set out to protect. Note yorkie-store's `normalizeCell` (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:241-251) deliberately treats spill fields as content, so the two notions of 'empty' disagree.

finding.summary: Decrease no-op guard (`selectionRendersAt`) inspects only raw values, so a Decrease press does nothing while other selected cells visibly render decimals via their number format
finding.evidence: `changeDecimals` line 4198: `if (stepped < 0 && !explicitDp && (await this.selectionRendersAt(0))) return;`. `selectionRendersAt` (4246-4261) only looks at `cell.v` via `decimalsInValue`, never at the cell's effective `nf`/`dp`. Scenario: A1 = '12' plain (active, valueDp 0, no explicit dp) and B1 = '12' with `nf: 'number'` (renders '12.00'). Selecting A1:B1 and pressing Decrease returns early — B1 keeps showing two decimals even though it has decimals to drop. The comment on the guard explicitly claims the check "has to look past the active cell: a neighbour that still shows decimals has something to lose", but a neighbour that shows decimals only because of its format is missed.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as written. sheet.ts:4198 gates the Decrease no-op on `selectionRendersAt(0)`, and that helper (sheet.ts:4246-4261) inspects only `cell.v` via `decimalsInValue` (format.ts:92-98, pure string scan) — it never reads `cell.s`, `resolveEffectiveStyle`, or `formatValue`, unlike the sibling `unsetKeepsRendering` (sheet.ts:4275-4302) which does. Since `formatValue` uses `dp ?? 2` for `nf: 'number'` (format.ts:119, 124-131), a neighbour cell `v: '12'` with `nf: 'number'` and no explicit `dp` renders '12.00' yet reports 0 raw decimals, so with a plain active cell A1='12' (getActiveDecimalState -> dp 0, explicitDp false, sheet.ts:4165-4186) the guard returns early and the whole selection is left untouched; without it the code would write `{dp: 0, nf: 'number'}` (sheet.ts:4208-4235) and correctly drop B1's decimals. The path is reachable directly from the UI handlers (spreadsheet.ts:536, 546) with no other pre-check, and the design doc (docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:269-271) states the opposite intended behavior ("if another selected cell still shows decimals, the step is written after all"). Existing tests only cover the raw-value neighbour case (decimals.test.ts:145-158), not the format-only case. Real, user-visible dead-button logic bug in the Correctness lane; no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: `unsetKeepsRendering` formats every selected cell with the ACTIVE cell's `nf`, ignoring each cell's own effective format, so an unset can be approved that changes another cell's rendering
finding.evidence: Lines 4290-4296 compute `effective = this.resolveEffectiveStyle(...)` but use only `effective?.cu`; the comparison uses the active cell's `nf`/`nfAfter` for every cell. If the active cell has `dp` with plain/undefined `nf` (nf param undefined → both sides return the raw value, always equal) while a neighbour carries `nf: 'percent'` (or 'currency') with the same stored `dp`, the check passes and `unsetRangeStyleValues({dp})` strips that neighbour's `dp` (its style verdict is 'match' since only `dp` is requested). The neighbour then falls back to the format's default 2 decimals instead of the requested `target`, so the step silently renders it wrong (e.g. target 3 → neighbour still shows 2).

verdict.reason: The code matches the finding. `unsetKeepsRendering` (sheet.ts:4275-4302) takes `nf` from the ACTIVE cell (`getActiveDecimalState`, sheet.ts:4196/4171-4185) and uses that same `nf`/`nfAfter` for every cell in the loop; the per-cell `resolveEffectiveStyle` result at 4291 is used only for `effective?.cu` (4292), while real rendering uses each cell's own `effective.nf`/`effective.dp` (sheet.ts:966-969). When the active cell has explicit `dp` with `nf` undefined/'plain', `formatValue` returns the raw value on both sides regardless of `dp` (format.ts:111-113), so the guard returns true unconditionally. `changeDecimals` then calls `unsetRangeStyleValues({dp})` (sheet.ts:4224-4228), and `verdictFor` treats a neighbour cell style such as `{nf:'percent', dp:N}` as 'match' since only `dp` is requested (sheet.ts:4361-4369), stripping its `dp` (4425-4428). That neighbour then renders the format's default 2 decimals instead of `target` — exactly the currency/percent case the doc comment at 4267-4273 claims is refused. The precondition (explicit `dp` with plain/absent `nf`) is reachable: the reset-formatting patch sets `nf:'plain'` without clearing `dp` (sheet.ts:144-158, applied at 3763) and `dp` is deliberately never pruned (style-mutation.ts:14-32). No caller-side guard limits the selection to a uniform format (selectionTargets, sheet.ts:4308-4312). Real logic bug plus silent style/data loss on neighbouring cells — blocking under the correctness rubric.

finding.summary: Decrease-decimals no-op guard inspects raw value precision, not the decimals actually rendered, so it silently swallows a legitimate step
finding.evidence: `changeDecimals` returns early when `stepped < 0 && !explicitDp && await this.selectionRendersAt(0)` (sheet.ts:4198). `selectionRendersAt` (sheet.ts:4246-4261) only compares `decimalsInValue(cell.v)` — the raw stored string — and ignores any `dp`/`nf` the cell carries. Concrete case: A1 empty (no style anywhere → `explicitDp=false`, `dp=0`), B1 holds value `'12'` with cell style `{nf:'number', dp:3}` (renders `12.000`). Select A1:B1 with A1 active and press Decrease: `decimalsInValue('12') === 0` for B1, so the guard reports "nothing to drop" and returns without writing, even though B1 visibly shows three decimals and should step to two. The guard's own comment claims it exists precisely to catch "a neighbour that still shows decimals", but it measures the value, not what is shown.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. changeDecimals (sheet.ts:4195-4204) returns early when `stepped < 0 && !explicitDp && await this.selectionRendersAt(0)`, and selectionRendersAt (sheet.ts:4246-4261) only compares `decimalsInValue(cell.v)`, a raw-string digit count (format.ts:92-98), ignoring the cell's own/inherited `dp`/`nf`. `explicitDp` is derived solely from the active cell (sheet.ts:4171-4185), so an empty/unstyled active cell gives dp=0 and triggers the guard; a neighbour holding value '12' with style {nf:'number', dp:3} renders '12.000' (format.ts:124-131) but reports 0 decimals, so the guard reports "nothing to drop" and no write occurs — directly contradicting its own comment that "a neighbour that still shows decimals ... takes the write below". The sibling helper unsetKeepsRendering (sheet.ts:4275-4302) demonstrates the render-aware resolution (resolveEffectiveStyle + formatValue) that selectionRendersAt lacks. The path is user-reachable via Spreadsheet.decreaseDecimals (view/spreadsheet.ts:544-548), and no guard elsewhere prevents it (selectionTargets, sheet.ts:4308-4312, just returns the selection). The reviewer's only misstatement is the expected result (the write applies target 0, not 2), which does not affect the defect: a legitimate, visible decrease step is silently swallowed. In-lane as a wrong-condition/dropped-operation correctness bug.
